# Validation of the ozone exposure {#sec-ozone-validation}

```{r}
#| label: setup-ozone-validation
#| include: false
source(here::here("Code", "00_setup.R"))
source(here::here("Code", "01_functions.R"))
source(here::here("Code", "02_plot_style.R"))
library(knitr)
theme_set(theme_report())
options(knitr.kable.NA = "")

read_table <- function(file) fread(file.path(dir_tables, file), encoding = "UTF-8")
fmt <- function(x, digits = 1) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = digits, big.mark = ",")
study_years <- get_param("study", "years")
warm_months <- get_param("study", "warm_season_months")

station_daily <- fread(derived_path("ozone_station_daily.csv"), encoding = "UTF-8")
station_daily[, date := as.Date(date)]
author <- new.env()
load(input_path("station_series"), envir = author)
author_series <- as.data.table(sf::st_drop_geometry(author$imputed_series))[
  , .(station, date, author_o3 = daily_o3)]
inputs <- merge(station_daily, author_series, by = c("station", "date"), all = TRUE)
inputs <- inputs[year(date) >= study_years[1] & year(date) <= study_years[2]]
inputs[, warm_season := is_warm_season(date, warm_months)]

by_station <- read_table("validation_inputs_by_station.csv")
by_level <- read_table("validation_inputs_by_level.csv")
loso <- read_table("validation_loso_overall.csv")
loso_common <- read_table("validation_loso_common.csv")
loso_station <- read_table("validation_loso_by_station.csv")
loso_high <- read_table("validation_loso_high_ozone.csv")
municipal_level <- read_table("validation_municipal_by_level.csv")
municipal_flags <- read_table("validation_municipal_flags.csv")
cams <- read_table("validation_cams_correlation.csv")

metric_label <- c(mean24 = "24-hour mean", mda8 = "MDA8")
method_label <- c(idw = "IDW", ok = "Ordinary kriging")
all_warm <- by_station[period == "warm season" & station == "All stations"]
top <- by_level[level == "D10"]
```

## What is validated

*Scripts: `Code/12_ozone_station_series.R` (station series and rebuilt
municipal series), `Code/14_interpolation_validation.R` (cross-validation
predictions), `Code/16_reanalysis_comparison.R` (reanalysis) and
`Code/17_validation_summary.R` (tables). Each part names its tables.*

The ozone exposure of the study is a daily value per municipality, interpolated
from the monitoring stations of the SINCA network. Three things can go wrong on
the way from the monitors to that value, and each is examined here:

A. **The station inputs.** Are the station series that feed the interpolation
   faithful to the measurements?
B. **The interpolation model.** How well do inverse distance weighting (IDW)
   and ordinary kriging predict ozone at a place without a monitor?
C. **The municipal series.** How much do the delivered series differ from
   series rebuilt from the measurements, in particular on high-ozone days?

A last section compares the series with an independent source, the CAMS
reanalysis, which assimilates satellite ozone retrievals.

The delivered series comes from `pollution-interpolation-kriging-idw`. Its
station inputs are hourly SINCA records trimmed at their 1st and 99th
percentiles, averaged over the day when at least 12 hours are valid, and
completed by imputation. Its interpolation uses IDW (power 2, at most 5
stations within 15 km) and ordinary kriging with a variogram fitted every day.
The validation uses the hourly SINCA records as published, with the validation
status of every record, for the 11 ozone stations of the Metropolitan Region.

## A. Station inputs {#sec-validation-inputs}

*Script: `Code/17_validation_summary.R`, from
`Data/Derived/ozone_station_daily.csv` (`Code/12_ozone_station_series.R`) and
the station series of the data author. Tables:
`Output/Tables/validation_inputs_by_station.csv` and
`validation_inputs_by_level.csv`. The scatter plot is computed in this page
from the same two series.*

The station series published with the interpolation code (2009-2020) are
compared, station by station and day by day, with the 24-hour mean computed
from the validated hourly records with the same rule of at least 12 valid
hours. A station-day is *identical* when the two values agree, *modified* when
both exist and differ, and has *no validated daily mean* when the author's
series holds a value that the validated records cannot produce (imputed, or
built on records never validated).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-inputs
#| tbl-cap: "Author's station series against the validated hourly records, warm seasons 2009-2020."
kable(by_station[period == "warm season",
                 .(station, station_days, identical_pct, modified_pct, no_validated_mean_pct,
                   mean_observed, mean_author_same_days, mean_change_when_modified)],
      digits = 1, format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
      col.names = c("Station", "Station-days", "Identical (%)", "Modified (%)",
                    "No validated daily mean (%)", "Observed mean (ppb)",
                    "Author's mean, same days (ppb)", "Mean change when modified (ppb)"))
```

In the warm season `r fmt(all_warm$modified_pct)`% of the station-days were
modified and `r fmt(all_warm$no_validated_mean_pct)`% have no validated daily
mean. The modifications are not spread evenly: they concentrate on the days
with most ozone.

```{r}
#| label: fig-level
#| fig-cap: "Author's station series against the observed 24-hour mean, by tenths of the observed value. Warm-season station-days with both values."
#| fig-height: 3.8
level_long <- melt(by_level[, .(level, `Observed` = observed_mean24, `Author's series` = author_mean)],
                   id.vars = "level", variable.name = "series", value.name = "ozone")
level_long[, level := factor(level, levels = paste0("D", 1:10))]
ggplot(level_long, aes(level, ozone, colour = series, group = series)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Observed" = "#2a78d6", "Author's series" = "#eb6834")) +
  labs(x = "Tenth of the observed 24-hour mean (D1 lowest, D10 highest)",
       y = "Ozone, 24-hour mean (ppb)", colour = NULL)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-level
#| tbl-cap: "Values behind the figure, with the observed MDA8 of the same days and the share of modified station-days."
kable(by_level, digits = 1, format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
      col.names = c("Tenth", "Station-days", "Observed 24-hour mean (ppb)", "Observed MDA8 (ppb)",
                    "Author's mean (ppb)", "Difference (ppb)", "Modified (%)"))
```

On the tenth of station-days with most ozone the author's series is
`r fmt(abs(top$difference))` ppb lower than the measurements
(`r fmt(top$author_mean)` against `r fmt(top$observed_mean24)` ppb, a
`r fmt(100 * abs(top$difference) / top$observed_mean24, 0)`% reduction), and
`r fmt(top$modified_pct, 0)`% of those station-days were modified. This is what
trimming the hourly values at their 99th percentile does to ozone: the hours it
removes are the afternoon peaks of the hottest days, so the daily mean of
exactly those days is pulled down. The trimming flattens the upper tail of the
exposure that the study is about.

```{r}
#| label: fig-scatter
#| fig-cap: "Author's station series against the observed 24-hour mean, warm-season station-days 2009-2020. The line is equality."
#| fig-height: 4.4
#| fig-width: 5.4
both <- inputs[warm_season == TRUE & !is.na(author_o3) & !is.na(mean24)]
ggplot(both, aes(mean24, author_o3)) +
  geom_bin2d(bins = 80) +
  geom_abline(colour = ink$primary, linewidth = 0.4) +
  scale_fill_magnitude(name = "Station-days", trans = "log10") +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(x = "Observed 24-hour mean (ppb)", y = "Author's series (ppb)") +
  theme(legend.position = "right", legend.justification = "center")
```

### Records that were never validated

*Computed in this page from the hourly file of the station, with
`read_sinca_hourly()` and `daily_from_hourly()` of `Code/01_functions.R`.*

SINCA marks every hourly record as validated, preliminary or not validated.
Most records of the study period are validated, but some station-periods were
never validated, and one of them is an evident instrument failure.

```{r}
#| label: fig-independencia
#| fig-cap: "Independencia, 2015-2017, monthly mean of the 24-hour ozone: hourly records of any status, the author's series, and the mean of the other stations in the author's series. Shaded: months in which Independencia has no validated record."
#| fig-height: 3.8
rules <- get_param("station_series")
codes <- fread(here::here(rules$stations_file), encoding = "UTF-8")
any_status <- daily_from_hourly(
  read_sinca_hourly(file.path(input_path("sinca_hourly_dir"),
                              sprintf(rules$hourly_file_pattern, codes[station == "Independencia", sinca_id])),
                    accepted_status = c("validated", "preliminary", "not_validated")),
  min_hours = rules$min_valid_hours_day, mda8_min_hours = rules$mda8_min_hours_window,
  mda8_min_windows = rules$mda8_min_windows_day
)[, .(date, any_status = mean24)]
window <- merge(inputs[date >= as.Date("2015-01-01") & date <= as.Date("2017-12-31")],
                any_status, by = "date", all.x = TRUE)
window[, month_start := as.Date(format(date, "%Y-%m-01"))]
monthly <- window[, .(
  `Independencia, records of any status` = mean(any_status[station == "Independencia"], na.rm = TRUE),
  `Independencia, author's series` = mean(author_o3[station == "Independencia"], na.rm = TRUE),
  `Other stations, author's series` = mean(author_o3[station != "Independencia"], na.rm = TRUE),
  validated_days = sum(station == "Independencia" & !is.na(mean24))
), by = month_start]
shade <- monthly[validated_days == 0, .(xmin = month_start, xmax = month_start + 31)]
monthly_long <- melt(monthly, id.vars = "month_start", measure.vars = 2:4,
                     variable.name = "series", value.name = "ozone")
no_validated <- inputs[station == "Independencia" & year(date) == 2016 & is.na(mean24) & !is.na(author_o3), .N]
ggplot(monthly_long) +
  geom_rect(data = shade, aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf),
            fill = ink$grid, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_line(aes(month_start, ozone, colour = series), linewidth = 0.8) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Independencia, records of any status" = "#1baf7a",
                                 "Independencia, author's series" = "#eb6834",
                                 "Other stations, author's series" = ink$muted)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Ozone, 24-hour mean (ppb)", colour = NULL) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(nrow = 3))
```

From February 2016 the hourly records of the Independencia monitor fall far
below every other station and none of them was ever validated. The author's
series does not follow them: for the `r no_validated` days of 2016 without a
validated daily mean it holds imputed values, so that for most of that year
the station enters the interpolation as an estimate and not as a measurement.
The series rebuilt here use validated records only (`accepted_status` in the
configuration) and leave a station out of the days for which it has none, at
the cost of about 3% of the warm-season station-days.

## B. The interpolation model {#sec-validation-model}

*Scripts: `Code/14_interpolation_validation.R` (predictions, in
`Data/Derived/validation_loso_predictions.csv`) and
`Code/17_validation_summary.R`. Tables: `Output/Tables/validation_loso_overall.csv`,
`validation_loso_common.csv`, `validation_loso_by_station.csv` and
`validation_loso_high_ozone.csv`.*

Leave-one-station-out cross-validation: for every warm-season day of 2009-2020
each station is removed in turn, the model is fitted to the remaining stations
with the author's function and parameters, and the removed station is
predicted. The observed values are the validated 24-hour mean and MDA8.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-loso
#| tbl-cap: "Leave-one-station-out cross-validation, warm seasons 2009-2020. R² is the coefficient of determination against the 1:1 line."
loso_table <- copy(loso)[, `:=`(metric = metric_label[metric], method = method_label[method])]
kable(loso_table[, .(metric, method, n, mean_observed, bias, mae, rmse, nrmse_pct, pearson_r, r2,
                     not_predicted_pct, interval_coverage_pct)],
      digits = c(0, 0, 0, 1, 2, 2, 2, 1, 3, 3, 1, 1), format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
      col.names = c("Metric", "Method", "Station-days", "Observed mean (ppb)", "Bias (ppb)",
                    "MAE (ppb)", "RMSE (ppb)", "RMSE (% of mean)", "Pearson r", "R²",
                    "Not predicted (%)", "Inside the 95% kriging interval (%)"))
```

IDW gives no value when no station lies within its 15 km radius, which is
always the case for Talagante and sometimes for other stations when their
neighbours have no validated record; kriging always gives one. The table above
therefore compares the methods on different station-days. On the station-days
that both methods predict:

```{r}
#| label: tbl-loso-common
#| tbl-cap: "The two methods on the same station-days."
common_table <- copy(loso_common)[, `:=`(metric = metric_label[metric], method = method_label[method])]
kable(common_table[order(metric, method), .(metric, method, n, bias, mae, rmse, nrmse_pct, pearson_r, r2)],
      digits = c(0, 0, 0, 2, 2, 2, 1, 3, 3), format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
      col.names = c("Metric", "Method", "Station-days", "Bias (ppb)", "MAE (ppb)", "RMSE (ppb)",
                    "RMSE (% of mean)", "Pearson r", "R²"))
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-loso-station
#| fig-cap: "Cross-validation error by station: RMSE as a percentage of the station mean."
#| fig-height: 4.6
station_plot <- copy(loso_station)[, `:=`(metric = metric_label[metric], method = method_label[method])]
order_station <- station_plot[metric == "MDA8" & method == "IDW"][order(nrmse_pct), station]
ggplot(station_plot, aes(nrmse_pct, factor(station, levels = order_station), colour = method)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.4) +
  facet_wrap(~metric) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = colour_method) +
  labs(x = "RMSE (% of the station mean)", y = NULL, colour = NULL)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-loso-station
#| tbl-cap: "Cross-validation by station."
kableExtra::scroll_box(
  kableExtra::kable_styling(
    kable(station_plot[order(metric, station, method),
                       .(metric, station, method, n, mean_observed, bias, rmse, pearson_r, r2)],
          format = "html", digits = c(0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 2, 2, 3, 3), format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
          col.names = c("Metric", "Station", "Method", "Station-days", "Observed mean (ppb)",
                        "Bias (ppb)", "RMSE (ppb)", "Pearson r", "R²")),
    bootstrap_options = c("striped", "condensed"), font_size = 12),
  height = "380px"
)
```

### High-ozone days

The analysis classifies days as high ozone against a percentile of each place.
The same is done here with the predictions: a station-day is predicted high
when the prediction exceeds the percentile of the predictions at that station.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-loso-high
#| tbl-cap: "High-ozone days: predicted against observed classification at the station left out."
high_table <- copy(loso_high)[, `:=`(metric = metric_label[metric], method = method_label[method])]
kable(high_table[order(metric, percentile, method),
                 .(metric, percentile = paste0("> P", percentile), method, n,
                   sensitivity = 100 * sensitivity, specificity = 100 * specificity,
                   agreement = 100 * agreement, kappa)],
      digits = c(0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 1, 2), format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
      col.names = c("Metric", "Cut-off", "Method", "Station-days", "Sensitivity (%)",
                    "Specificity (%)", "Agreement (%)", "Kappa"))
```

## C. Delivered and rebuilt municipal series {#sec-validation-municipal}

*Scripts: `Code/12_ozone_station_series.R` (rebuilt series) and
`Code/17_validation_summary.R`. Tables: `Output/Tables/validation_reproduction.csv`,
`validation_municipal_by_level.csv` and `validation_municipal_flags.csv`.*

Script 12 interpolates the validated station values to the 33 municipalities
with the same model: `o3obs` is the 24-hour mean and `o3mda8` the daily maximum
8-hour mean.

First, a reproduction test. On the days when every station value of the
author's series equals the validated 24-hour mean, the two municipal series
have the same inputs and should coincide if this project runs the same
interpolation.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-reproduction
#| tbl-cap: "Rebuilt against delivered municipal ozone on the warm-season days with identical station inputs."
reproduction <- read_table("validation_reproduction.csv")
kable(reproduction[, .(method = method_label[method], days, municipality_days, within_0.001_ppb_pct,
                       median_abs_difference, max_abs_difference)],
      digits = c(0, 0, 0, 1, 6, 4), format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
      col.names = c("Method", "Days", "Municipality-days", "Within 0.001 ppb (%)",
                    "Median absolute difference (ppb)", "Largest absolute difference (ppb)"))
```

With the same inputs this project returns the delivered values: all of the IDW
values and nearly all of the kriging values agree to the third decimal (the
daily variogram fit makes kriging sensitive to the last digits of its inputs).
The differences shown in the rest of this section therefore come from the
station inputs.

```{r}
#| label: fig-municipal-level
#| fig-cap: "Delivered against rebuilt 24-hour mean by tenths of the rebuilt value, municipality-days of the warm seasons 2009-2020."
#| fig-height: 3.8
ml <- melt(municipal_level[, .(method = method_label[method], level,
                               `Rebuilt from validated records` = rebuilt_mean24,
                               `Delivered` = delivered_mean24)],
           id.vars = c("method", "level"), variable.name = "series", value.name = "ozone")
ml[, level := factor(level, levels = paste0("D", 1:10))]
ggplot(ml, aes(level, ozone, colour = series, group = series)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~method) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Rebuilt from validated records" = "#2a78d6", "Delivered" = "#eb6834")) +
  labs(x = "Tenth of the rebuilt 24-hour mean (D1 lowest, D10 highest)",
       y = "Ozone, 24-hour mean (ppb)", colour = NULL)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-municipal-level
#| tbl-cap: "Values behind the figure, with the rebuilt MDA8 of the same municipality-days."
kable(municipal_level[, .(method = method_label[method], level, municipality_days, rebuilt_mean24,
                          delivered_mean24, difference, rebuilt_mda8)],
      digits = 1, format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
      col.names = c("Method", "Tenth", "Municipality-days", "Rebuilt 24-hour mean (ppb)",
                    "Delivered (ppb)", "Difference (ppb)", "Rebuilt MDA8 (ppb)"))
```

### Does the choice of series change who is exposed?

```{r}
#| label: tbl-flags
#| tbl-cap: "Agreement of the high-ozone flags between series, municipality-days of the warm seasons 2009-2020. Sensitivity and specificity take the first series as reference."
series_label <- c(o3 = "Delivered 24-hour mean", o3obs = "Rebuilt 24-hour mean", o3mda8 = "Rebuilt MDA8")
flags <- copy(municipal_flags)[, `:=`(reference = series_label[reference], compared = series_label[compared],
                                      method = method_label[method])]
kable(flags[, .(reference, compared, method, percentile = paste0("> P", percentile), pearson_r,
                sensitivity = 100 * sensitivity, specificity = 100 * specificity,
                agreement = 100 * agreement, kappa)],
      digits = c(0, 0, 0, 0, 2, 1, 1, 1, 2),
      col.names = c("Reference", "Compared", "Method", "Cut-off", "Pearson r", "Sensitivity (%)",
                    "Specificity (%)", "Agreement (%)", "Kappa"))
```

## An independent source: the CAMS reanalysis {#sec-validation-cams}

*Script: `Code/16_reanalysis_comparison.R`. Tables:
`Output/Tables/validation_cams_correlation.csv` and `validation_cams_cells.csv`
(the cells of the reanalysis that hold the municipalities).*

No satellite measures ozone at the surface with the resolution of a city: the
ozone column seen from space is dominated by the stratosphere. The closest
independent source is a reanalysis that assimilates the satellite retrievals
into a chemistry model. CAMS EAC4 has cells of 0.75 degrees, so the 33
municipalities fall in two cells and the comparison says nothing about
differences between municipalities. What it can check is whether the
day-to-day course of ozone over the city in the station-based series is also
seen by a source that does not use the monitors.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-cams
#| tbl-cap: "City-wide daily ozone against CAMS EAC4, warm seasons 2009-2020. Anomalies are deviations from the mean of each calendar month."
cams_series <- c(o3_idw = "Delivered 24-hour mean, IDW", o3_ok = "Delivered 24-hour mean, kriging",
                 o3obs_idw = "Rebuilt 24-hour mean, IDW", o3obs_ok = "Rebuilt 24-hour mean, kriging",
                 o3mda8_idw = "Rebuilt MDA8, IDW", o3mda8_ok = "Rebuilt MDA8, kriging")
cams_table <- copy(cams)[, `:=`(series = cams_series[series],
                                cams = fifelse(cams == "cams_mean24", "Daily mean", "Afternoon (15 and 18 h)"))]
kable(cams_table, digits = c(0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 2, 2), format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
      col.names = c("Station-based series", "CAMS value", "Days", "Series mean (ppb)",
                    "CAMS mean (ppb)", "Correlation, daily values", "Correlation, anomalies"))
```

CAMS is a weak reference for surface ozone in a basin that one of its cells
covers almost entirely, mountains included: its values are much higher than
the monitors and the correlations are modest. Within those limits, the series
rebuilt from validated records follow it more closely than the delivered
series, and the MDA8 more closely than the 24-hour mean.

## What this means for the analysis {#sec-validation-conclusions}

*Drawn from the tables of the parts above; the number of stations behind the
delivered series comes from the exposure dataset.*

```{r}
#| label: conclusions
# Stations behind the delivered ozone on the days of analysis
stations_per_day <- fread(derived_path("exposure_2009_2020.csv"),
                          select = c("in_study_period", "warm_season", "o3_n_stations"))[
  in_study_period == TRUE & warm_season == TRUE, range(o3_n_stations)]
common_wide <- dcast(loso_common, metric ~ method, value.var = c("rmse", "r2"))
mda8_flags <- municipal_flags[reference == "o3mda8" & compared == "o3" & method == "idw"]
coverage <- loso[method == "ok", .(metric, interval_coverage_pct)]
las_condes <- loso_station[station == "Las Condes" & metric == "mda8" & method == "ok"]
top_municipal <- municipal_level[method == "idw" & level == "D10"]
```

1. **The delivered series understates the days with most ozone.** Its station
   inputs are `r fmt(abs(top$difference))` ppb below the measurements on the
   highest tenth of station-days, and its municipal values are
   `r fmt(abs(top_municipal$difference))` ppb below the rebuilt ones on the
   highest tenth of municipality-days. A study of high-ozone days and of their
   interaction with heat should not use inputs trimmed at the 99th percentile.
2. **Station-days without a validated measurement are estimates.** In the
   delivered series `r fmt(all_warm$no_validated_mean_pct)`% of the warm-season
   station-days have no validated daily mean; the Independencia monitor, which
   failed in 2016, is carried by imputed values for most of that year. The
   rebuilt series use validated records only.
3. **The metric matters.** The plan names the MDA8; the delivered series is a
   24-hour mean. Among the municipality-days above the 75th percentile of
   MDA8, the delivered 24-hour mean flags
   `r fmt(100 * mda8_flags[percentile == 75, sensitivity], 0)`% as high ozone
   (kappa `r fmt(mda8_flags[percentile == 75, kappa], 2)`).
4. **Interpolation method.** On the same station-days ordinary kriging has
   the lower cross-validation error for both metrics: RMSE
   `r fmt(common_wide[metric == "mean24", rmse_ok], 2)` against
   `r fmt(common_wide[metric == "mean24", rmse_idw], 2)` ppb for the 24-hour
   mean and `r fmt(common_wide[metric == "mda8", rmse_ok], 2)` against
   `r fmt(common_wide[metric == "mda8", rmse_idw], 2)` ppb for the MDA8. The
   difference is clear for the 24-hour mean and small for the MDA8. The kriging
   intervals contain the left-out observation
   `r paste(sprintf("%s%% of the time for the %s", fmt(coverage$interval_coverage_pct, 0), metric_label[coverage$metric]), collapse = " and ")`,
   against a nominal 95%, so they should not be read as measurement
   uncertainty. The working value of the configuration is still IDW; this
   result argues for kriging and the choice is open.
5. **What interpolation cannot fix.** Between `r stations_per_day[1]` and
   `r stations_per_day[2]` monitors a day describe 33 municipalities in the
   delivered series, and the error is far from uniform. Las Condes, the station
   with most ozone, cannot be predicted from the others (bias
   `r fmt(las_condes$bias)` ppb when it is left out): the eastern
   municipalities depend on that single monitor. The cross-validation error is
   the error at a monitored site when its own monitor is ignored; it is the
   best available estimate of the error in municipalities without a monitor,
   not a guarantee.

The exposure dataset keeps the three series (`o3`, `o3obs`, `o3mda8`) so that
the choice can be made by the principal investigator and its effect shown as a
sensitivity analysis. The working value in the configuration is still the
delivered series.

# Municipal maps and time series of single and compound exposure {#sec-maps-trends}

```{r}
#| label: setup-maps-trends
#| include: false
source(here::here("Code", "00_setup.R"))
source(here::here("Code", "01_functions.R"))
source(here::here("Code", "02_plot_style.R"))
library(knitr)
library(sf)
theme_set(theme_report())
options(knitr.kable.NA = "")

read_table <- function(file) fread(file.path(dir_tables, file), encoding = "UTF-8")
exposure <- fread(derived_path("exposure_2009_2020.csv"), encoding = "UTF-8")
exposure[, date := as.Date(date)]
analysis <- exposure[in_study_period == TRUE & warm_season == TRUE]

heatwave_main <- get_param("models", "heatwave_main")
ozone_main <- paste0(get_param("air_pollution", "ozone_series_main"), "_",
                     get_param("air_pollution", "interpolation_method_main"))
cutoff_main <- get_param("models", "ozone_cutoff_main")
ozone_flag_main <- paste0(ozone_main, "_gt_p", cutoff_main)

shapes_env <- new.env()
load(input_path("municipality_shapes"), envir = shapes_env)
shapes <- shapes_env$comunas_santiago[, c("cod_comuna", "comuna")]
shapes$com <- as.integer(shapes$cod_comuna)
stopifnot(setequal(shapes$com, study_municipalities()$code))

map_values <- function(values, value_column, title, legend, hue = "blue", digits = 1) {
  data <- merge(shapes, values, by = "com")
  ggplot(data) +
    geom_sf(aes(fill = .data[[value_column]]), colour = "#ffffff", linewidth = 0.25) +
    scale_fill_magnitude(name = legend, hue = hue,
                         labels = function(x) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = digits)) +
    labs(title = title) +
    theme_map()
}
fmt <- function(x, digits = 0) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = digits, big.mark = ",")
```

## Scope

Distribution of the single exposures (temperature, heatwaves, ozone) and of the
compound exposure (a heatwave day with high ozone) across the 33 municipalities
and the warm seasons of 2009 to 2020. All figures use the days between
1 November and 31 March.

Where one definition has to be shown, this section uses the working definitions of
`config/config.yml`: heatwave `r heatwave_main`, ozone series `r ozone_main`,
high ozone above the `r cutoff_main`th percentile of the municipality. They are
working values, not final choices; the grid of definitions covers every
combination.

The first sections describe the municipalities as a group. The series of every
municipality, and of the mean of the 33, over the whole study period are in
[Time series of every municipality and of their mean](#sec-series-municipalities).

## Single exposures

*Computed in this page from the exposure dataset
(`Code/13_exposure_merge_qc.R`). The maps use the municipal polygons of the
interpolation repository.*

```{r}
#| label: tbl-descriptive
#| tbl-cap: "Exposure variables over the municipality-days of the warm seasons 2009-2020."
variables <- c(tmax = "Maximum temperature (°C)", tmin = "Minimum temperature (°C)",
               o3_idw = "Ozone, delivered 24-hour mean, IDW (ppb)",
               o3_ok = "Ozone, delivered 24-hour mean, kriging (ppb)",
               o3obs_idw = "Ozone, rebuilt 24-hour mean, IDW (ppb)",
               o3mda8_idw = "Ozone, rebuilt MDA8, IDW (ppb)",
               o3mda8_ok = "Ozone, rebuilt MDA8, kriging (ppb)",
               pm25_idw = "PM2.5, IDW (µg/m³)", no2_idw = "Nitrogen dioxide, IDW (ppb)",
               hum_idw = "Relative humidity, IDW (%)")
descriptive <- rbindlist(lapply(names(variables), function(v) {
  x <- analysis[[v]]
  q <- quantile(x, c(0.05, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.95), na.rm = TRUE)
  data.table(variable = variables[[v]], n = sum(!is.na(x)), missing = sum(is.na(x)),
             mean = mean(x, na.rm = TRUE), sd = sd(x, na.rm = TRUE),
             p5 = q[1], p25 = q[2], median = q[3], p75 = q[4], p95 = q[5])
}))
kable(descriptive, digits = 1, format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
      col.names = c("Variable", "N", "Missing", "Mean", "SD", "P5", "P25", "Median", "P75", "P95"))
```

### Time series {#sec-time-series}

```{r}
#| label: fig-annual
#| fig-cap: "Warm-season means by calendar year. Line: median of the 33 municipalities; band: range between municipalities."
#| fig-height: 6.5
annual <- analysis[, .(tmax = mean(tmax), o3 = mean(get(ozone_main), na.rm = TRUE),
                       mda8 = mean(o3mda8_idw, na.rm = TRUE)), by = .(com, year)]
annual_long <- melt(annual, id.vars = c("com", "year"))
annual_long[, variable := factor(variable, levels = c("tmax", "o3", "mda8"),
  labels = c("Maximum temperature (°C)", "Ozone, 24-hour mean (ppb)", "Ozone, MDA8 (ppb)"))]
bands <- annual_long[, .(median = median(value), low = min(value), high = max(value)),
                     by = .(variable, year)]
ggplot(bands, aes(year)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = low, ymax = high), fill = ramp_blue[2], alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_line(aes(y = median), colour = ramp_blue[6], linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(aes(y = median), colour = ramp_blue[6], size = 1.8) +
  facet_wrap(~variable, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2009:2020) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL,
       caption = "Calendar years: January to March and November to December of each year.")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-heatwave-years
#| fig-cap: "Heatwave days per municipality by calendar year, percentile definitions with two or more consecutive days."
#| fig-height: 3.8
hw_years <- melt(analysis[, lapply(.SD, function(x) sum(x) / uniqueN(com)), by = year,
                          .SDcols = c("hw_p90_2d", "hw_p95_2d", "hw_p99_2d")],
                 id.vars = "year", variable.name = "indicator", value.name = "days")
hw_years[, indicator := factor(indicator, levels = c("hw_p90_2d", "hw_p95_2d", "hw_p99_2d"),
                               labels = c("> P90, 2 days", "> P95, 2 days", "> P99, 2 days"))]
ggplot(hw_years, aes(year, days, colour = indicator)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(size = 1.8) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("> P90, 2 days" = "#2a78d6", "> P95, 2 days" = "#eb6834",
                                 "> P99, 2 days" = "#1baf7a")) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2009:2020) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Heatwave days per municipality", colour = NULL)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-months
#| fig-cap: "Seasonal profile: mean of the 33 municipalities by month of the warm season, 2009-2020."
#| fig-height: 3.6
monthly <- analysis[, .(tmax = mean(tmax), o3 = mean(get(ozone_main), na.rm = TRUE),
                        mda8 = mean(o3mda8_idw, na.rm = TRUE),
                        hw = 100 * mean(get(heatwave_main))), by = .(month = month(date))]
monthly_long <- melt(monthly, id.vars = "month")
monthly_long[, month := factor(month, levels = c(11, 12, 1, 2, 3),
                               labels = c("Nov", "Dec", "Jan", "Feb", "Mar"))]
monthly_long[, variable := factor(variable, levels = c("tmax", "hw", "o3", "mda8"),
  labels = c("Maximum temperature (°C)", "Heatwave days (% of days)",
             "Ozone, 24-hour mean (ppb)", "Ozone, MDA8 (ppb)"))]
ggplot(monthly_long, aes(month, value, group = 1)) +
  geom_line(colour = ramp_blue[6], linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(colour = ramp_blue[6], size = 1.8) +
  facet_wrap(~variable, nrow = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL)
```

## Compound exposure

*Computed in this page from the exposure dataset, with `compound_category()`
of `Code/01_functions.R`. The definition is in
[Compound exposure](#sec-methods-compound).*

A municipality-day belongs to one of four categories: neither exposure (E00),
heatwave only (E10), high ozone only (E01), or both (E11).

```{r}
#| label: compound-main
analysis[, category := compound_category(get(heatwave_main), get(ozone_flag_main))]
labels <- c(E00 = "Neither", E01 = "High ozone only", E10 = "Heatwave only",
            E11 = "Heatwave and high ozone")
analysis[, category_label := factor(labels[as.character(category)], levels = labels)]
overall <- analysis[!is.na(category), .(days = .N), keyby = category_label]
overall[, share := 100 * days / sum(days)]
p_hw <- analysis[!is.na(category), mean(get(heatwave_main))]
p_oz <- analysis[!is.na(category), mean(get(ozone_flag_main))]
p_both <- analysis[!is.na(category), mean(category == "E11")]
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-compound
#| tbl-cap: "Municipality-days by compound exposure category, working definitions, warm seasons 2009-2020."
kable(overall, digits = 1, format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
      col.names = c("Category", "Municipality-days", "%"))
```

Heatwave days are `r fmt(100 * p_hw, 1)`% of the municipality-days and high-ozone
days `r fmt(100 * p_oz, 1)`%. If the two were independent, `r fmt(100 * p_hw * p_oz, 1)`%
of the days would have both; the observed share is `r fmt(100 * p_both, 1)`%,
`r fmt(p_both / (p_hw * p_oz), 1)` times the expected one.
`r fmt(100 * p_both / p_hw, 0)`% of the heatwave days are also high-ozone days.

### Maps

```{r}
#| label: fig-map-compound
#| fig-cap: "Compound exposure by municipality, working definitions, warm seasons 2009-2020. Left: days per year with a heatwave and high ozone. Right: share of heatwave days that are also high-ozone days."
#| fig-height: 4.8
#| fig-width: 9
compound_mun <- analysis[!is.na(category), .(
  compound_days = sum(category == "E11") / 12,
  share_of_heatwave = 100 * sum(category == "E11") / sum(get(heatwave_main))
), by = com]
patchwork::wrap_plots(
  map_values(compound_mun, "compound_days", "Compound days per year", "Days per year",
             hue = "orange"),
  map_values(compound_mun, "share_of_heatwave", "Heatwave days with high ozone", "%",
             digits = 0),
  ncol = 2
)
```

### Across the grid of definitions {#sec-grid-definitions}

*Script: `Code/13_exposure_merge_qc.R`. Tables:
`Output/Tables/compound_frequency_by_municipality.csv` and
`compound_frequency_by_year.csv`.*

Share of municipality-days with both exposures, for the 15 heatwave definitions
and the three ozone cut-offs, with the ozone series in use (`r ozone_main`).

```{r}
#| label: fig-grid
#| fig-cap: "Compound days (% of municipality-days) by heatwave definition and ozone cut-off."
#| fig-height: 5.6
grid <- read_table("compound_frequency_by_municipality.csv")
grid <- grid[grepl(paste0("^", ozone_main, "_gt_p"), ozone),
             .(e11 = sum(e11), e10 = sum(e10), e01 = sum(e01), classified = sum(days - not_classified)),
             by = .(heatwave, ozone)]
grid[, `:=`(share = 100 * e11 / classified,
            ratio = (e11 / classified) / (((e11 + e10) / classified) * ((e11 + e01) / classified)),
            cutoff = paste0("> P", sub(".*_gt_p", "", ozone)))]
grid[, heatwave := factor(heatwave, levels = rev(unique(heatwave)))]
ggplot(grid, aes(cutoff, heatwave, fill = share)) +
  geom_tile(colour = ink$surface, linewidth = 1) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.1f", share),
                colour = share > max(share) * 0.55), size = 3.2, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "#ffffff", `FALSE` = ink$primary)) +
  scale_fill_magnitude(name = "% of days", hue = "orange") +
  labs(x = "Ozone cut-off (municipality percentile)", y = NULL) +
  theme(panel.grid.major = element_blank(), legend.position = "right",
        legend.justification = "center")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-grid
#| tbl-cap: "Compound exposure across the grid: days with both exposures, and the ratio of the observed share to the share expected if heatwaves and high ozone were independent."
kableExtra::scroll_box(
  kableExtra::kable_styling(
    kable(grid[order(-as.integer(heatwave), cutoff),
               .(heatwave, cutoff, e11, share, e10, e01, ratio)],
          format = "html", digits = c(0, 0, 0, 2, 0, 0, 2), format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
          col.names = c("Heatwave", "Ozone cut-off", "Compound days (E11)", "% of days",
                        "Heatwave only (E10)", "High ozone only (E01)",
                        "Observed / expected")),
    bootstrap_options = c("striped", "condensed"), font_size = 12),
  height = "420px"
)
```

The frequency tables for every ozone series, by municipality and by year, are in
`Output/Tables/compound_frequency_by_municipality.csv` and
`Output/Tables/compound_frequency_by_year.csv`.

## Time series of every municipality and of their mean {#sec-series-municipalities}

*Script: `Code/18_exposure_time_series.R`. Tables, in `Output/Tables`:
`series_daily_all_municipalities.csv`, `series_monthly_by_municipality.csv`
and `series_annual_by_municipality.csv`. Figures, in `Output/Figures`:
`series_1_daily_temperature_ozone` to `series_7_municipalities_heatwave_days`,
each as PDF and as PNG at `r get_param("figures", "png_dpi")` dpi. The script
writes the tables and draws every figure from them; this page shows the
files.*

```{r}
#| label: setup-series
#| include: false
series_tables <- c(daily = "series_daily_all_municipalities.csv",
                   monthly = "series_monthly_by_municipality.csv",
                   annual = "series_annual_by_municipality.csv")
series_names <- c("series_1_daily_temperature_ozone", "series_2_daily_compound_exposure",
                  "series_3_monthly_by_municipality", "series_4_annual_by_municipality",
                  "series_5_municipalities_temperature", "series_6_municipalities_ozone",
                  "series_7_municipalities_heatwave_days")
series_figure <- function(name) {
  stopifnot(name %in% series_names)
  file.path(dir_figures, paste0(name, ".png"))
}
needed <- c(file.path(dir_tables, series_tables), series_figure(series_names))
if (!all(file.exists(needed))) {
  stop("Files written by Code/18_exposure_time_series.R are missing:\n  ",
       paste(needed[!file.exists(needed)], collapse = "\n  "),
       "\nRun source(\"Code/run_all.R\"), or that script alone, before rendering this page.",
       call. = FALSE)
}
series_daily <- read_table(series_tables[["daily"]])
series_daily[, date := as.Date(date)]
series_monthly <- read_table(series_tables[["monthly"]])
series_annual <- read_table(series_tables[["annual"]])
# The rows without a municipality code hold the mean of the municipalities
annual_mean <- series_annual[is.na(com)]
annual_municipal <- series_annual[!is.na(com)]
monthly_mean <- series_monthly[is.na(com)]
monthly_municipal <- series_monthly[!is.na(com)]
n_municipalities <- nrow(study_municipalities())
stopifnot(
  uniqueN(annual_municipal$com) == n_municipalities, uniqueN(monthly_municipal$com) == n_municipalities,
  nrow(annual_mean) == uniqueN(series_annual$year), all(series_daily$municipalities == n_municipalities),
  nrow(series_daily) == uniqueN(analysis$date)
)
long_table <- function(table, height = "420px") {
  kableExtra::scroll_box(
    kableExtra::kable_styling(table, bootstrap_options = c("striped", "condensed"), font_size = 12),
    height = height
  )
}
# One row per municipality and one column per year, the mean of the municipalities last
wide_by_year <- function(variable, digits) {
  wide <- dcast(series_annual, com + municipality ~ year, value.var = variable)
  setorder(wide, com, na.last = TRUE)
  long_table(kable(wide[, !"com"], format = "html", digits = digits,
                   col.names = c("Municipality", setdiff(names(wide), c("com", "municipality")))))
}

# Figures quoted in the text
heatwave_somewhere <- series_daily[with_heatwave > 0, .N]
heatwave_in_most <- series_daily[with_heatwave > municipalities / 2, .N]
heatwave_everywhere <- series_daily[with_heatwave == municipalities, .N]
compound_somewhere <- series_daily[heatwave_and_high_ozone > 0, .N]
compound_everywhere <- series_daily[heatwave_and_high_ozone == municipalities, .N]
# Years with more heatwave days than the mean of the twelve
heavy_years <- annual_mean[heatwave_days > mean(heatwave_days), year]
heavy_share <- annual_municipal[, 100 * sum(heatwave_days[year %in% heavy_years]) / sum(heatwave_days)]
# How closely each municipality follows the mean of the municipalities, month by month
monthly_reference <- monthly_mean[, .(year, month, tmax_mean = tmax, o3_mean = o3, mda8_mean = mda8)]
follows <- merge(monthly_municipal, monthly_reference, by = c("year", "month"))[
  , .(tmax = cor(tmax, tmax_mean), o3 = cor(o3, o3_mean), mda8 = cor(mda8, mda8_mean),
      tmax_difference = mean(tmax - tmax_mean)), by = municipality]
# The municipality and year with most high-ozone days
most_ozone <- annual_municipal[which.max(high_ozone_days)]
most_ozone_other_years <- annual_municipal[com == most_ozone$com & year != most_ozone$year]
# Quoted in "Points to settle", at the end of the page
ozone_point <- sprintf(
  "In the delivered series %s has %d high-ozone days in %d, against %d at most in its other years",
  most_ozone$municipality, most_ozone$high_ozone_days, most_ozone$year,
  max(most_ozone_other_years$high_ozone_days))
mda8_days_missing <- series_daily[mda8_municipalities < municipalities, .N]
mda8_days_empty <- series_daily[mda8_municipalities == 0, .N]
```

The figures and the tables above describe the municipalities as a group. This
section follows every municipality, and the mean of the 33, over the whole
study period: the `r fmt(nrow(series_daily))` days of the warm seasons of 2009
to 2020, by day, by month and by calendar year.

- **Definitions.** The working definitions of `config/config.yml`: heatwave
  `r heatwave_main` (`r heatwave_label(heatwave_main)`), ozone series
  `r ozone_main`, high ozone above the `r cutoff_main`th percentile of the
  municipality. The daily maximum 8-hour mean is the series rebuilt from the
  validated hourly records (`o3mda8_idw`).
- **Mean of the 33 municipalities.** The plain mean of the 33 municipal
  values: every municipality counts the same, whatever its population or its
  area.
- **Days without a value.** The delivered ozone has a value on every day of
  analysis. The rebuilt MDA8 is missing in at least one municipality on
  `r mda8_days_missing` days, on `r mda8_days_empty` of them in all: the means
  are taken over the municipalities, or the days, that have a value, and the
  tables written by the script give their number.

### What the series show

- **Heatwave days are concentrated in `r length(heavy_years)` years.** In
  `r paste(heavy_years, collapse = ", ")` the municipalities have between
  `r fmt(min(annual_mean[year %in% heavy_years, heatwave_days]))` and
  `r fmt(max(annual_mean[year %in% heavy_years, heatwave_days]))` heatwave days
  on average, against `r fmt(min(annual_mean[!year %in% heavy_years, heatwave_days]))`
  to `r fmt(max(annual_mean[!year %in% heavy_years, heatwave_days]))` days in the
  other years: those `r length(heavy_years)` years hold `r fmt(heavy_share)`% of
  the heatwave days of the period. The threshold comes from a reference period
  that ends in 2020, and the days above it are more frequent at the end of that
  period ([Heatwave definitions](#sec-methods-heatwaves)).
- **How many municipalities at once.** `r heatwave_somewhere` of the
  `r fmt(nrow(series_daily))` days have a heatwave in at least one
  municipality; on `r heatwave_in_most` of them in more than half of the
  municipalities, and on `r heatwave_everywhere` in all 33. A heatwave with
  high ozone reaches at least one municipality on `r compound_somewhere` days,
  and all of them on `r compound_everywhere`.
- **Temperature moves together, ozone less.** Month by month, the temperature
  of every municipality follows the mean of the 33: the lowest correlation is
  `r fmt(min(follows$tmax), 3)`
  (`r follows[which.min(tmax), municipality]`, whose series is also
  `r fmt(abs(follows[which.min(tmax), tmax_difference]), 1)` °C colder than
  the mean). For the delivered ozone the correlation goes from
  `r fmt(min(follows$o3), 2)` (`r follows[which.min(o3), municipality]`) to
  `r fmt(max(follows$o3), 2)` (`r follows[which.max(o3), municipality]`): the
  ozone of a municipality depends on the few monitors near it.
- **One series to look at.** `r most_ozone$municipality` has
  `r most_ozone$high_ozone_days` high-ozone days in `r most_ozone$year`,
  against `r max(most_ozone_other_years$high_ozone_days)` at most in its other
  years; its mean ozone of that year is `r fmt(most_ozone$o3, 1)` ppb, against
  `r fmt(min(most_ozone_other_years$o3), 1)` to
  `r fmt(max(most_ozone_other_years$o3), 1)` ppb in the others. The delivered
  series of that municipality and year should be checked against the station
  records before it is used.

# Points to settle {#sec-points-to-settle}

1. **29 February.** CR2MET has no leap days. They are filled by interpolation
   and flagged; the alternative is to leave them empty.
2. **Season of the percentiles.** All days of the year (reference code) or
   warm-season days only. The thresholds differ by about one degree.
3. **Heatwave indicators of the reference repository.** Its script counts
   consecutive days across stacked municipalities. This project counts them
   within each municipality.
4. **Fixed threshold of 30 °C.** With area-mean temperatures it is exceeded on
   `r hot30_most` and on `r hot30_least`.
5. **Ozone metric and inputs.** The delivered series is a 24-hour mean built on
   trimmed and imputed station series; the plan names the MDA8. See the
   [validation of the ozone exposure](#sec-ozone-validation).
6. **Negative kriging values.** Set to missing and counted in the tables above.
7. **Three buffer days of December 2008.** The monitoring network of PM2.5 and
   NO2 was smaller before 2009; those days only feed the lags of the first
   deaths of January 2009.
8. **Temperature of the municipalities that reach into the Andes.** The CR2MET
   series of a municipality describes its whole territory. `r andes_point`
   ([why](#sec-heatwave-municipalities)). The options: keep the series as it
   is; compute the temperature over the populated area, which needs the
   gridded CR2MET files; or repeat the models without that municipality as a
   sensitivity analysis.
9. **How the municipal CR2MET series were built.** The files do not say with
   which rule the grid was summarised over each territory
   ([Temperature](#sec-methods-temperature)). It should be confirmed with the
   team that produced them.
10. **One ozone series to check.** `r ozone_point`
    ([What the series show](#sec-series-municipalities)).

# R scripts {#sec-scripts}

The scripts are in [`Code/`](https://github.com/AmaruSimonAgueroJimenez/Heatwave-ozone-mortality-Chile/tree/main/Code) of the repository. They are
not executed when this page is rendered: `Code/run_all.R` runs them in order
and this page reads their outputs. The code of each one is folded below.

::: {.no-download}

| Script | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `Code/10_exposure_temperature.R` | The 15 heatwave indicators by municipality and day, from CR2MET. |
| `Code/11_exposure_air_pollution.R` | Daily ozone, PM2.5, NO2 and humidity by municipality, from the delivered interpolated SINCA series. |
| `Code/12_ozone_station_series.R` | Ozone rebuilt from the hourly SINCA records: 24-hour mean and MDA8 by station, interpolated to the municipalities. |
| `Code/13_exposure_merge_qc.R` | Exposure dataset 2009-2020, alignment checks, ozone categories, compound exposure frequencies. |
| `Code/14_interpolation_validation.R` | Leave-one-station-out cross-validation of IDW and ordinary kriging. |
| `Code/15_export_geodata.R` | Polygons, target points and station coordinates in open formats, for script 16 and for the pages in Python. |
| `Code/16_reanalysis_comparison.R` | Ozone series against the CAMS EAC4 reanalysis. |
| `Code/17_validation_summary.R` | Tables of the ozone validation: station inputs, cross-validation, delivered against rebuilt series. |
| `Code/18_exposure_time_series.R` | Time series of every municipality and of their mean over the whole study period: three tables and seven figures. |
| `Code/00_setup.R` | Packages, folders, parameters and checks of the inputs, shared by the scripts. |
| `Code/01_functions.R` | Functions shared by the scripts. |
| `Code/02_plot_style.R` | Style of the figures and the function that writes figure files. |

What each script reads and writes is in
[Workflow and scripts](#sec-methods-workflow).
